cases.text: The town was a compass, its needle fixed on the school; by dusk it became a lantern for the late walkers.
The town was a compass: its needle led every lost walker to the school; that same needle tore the school from the map.
Her apology was a bridge over the quarrel and a bandage over the same cut.
Her apology was a bridge inviting him across and a gate that barred him from the same conversation.
The archive was a mausoleum, but its open drawers made it a nursery for unfinished voices.
The archive was a mausoleum where the voices were buried and a nursery where those same voices had never been born.
At dawn the river was a blade; by noon, after the thaw, it was a ribbon carrying petals.
At dawn the river was a blade slicing the banks and a ribbon stitching those same banks shut.
His silence was a key: it locked the room against them and opened the pause where she could speak.
His silence was a key: it locked the only door, and it opened that same locked door.
The contract was a net for the deal and a map for the two signers, catching terms while showing their route.
The contract was a net trapping its two signers and a map proving those same signers were free.
The hallway was a spine holding the house upright and a throat carrying voices from room to room.
The promise was a rope pulling her home and a fence preventing her return to that same home.
The field was a scar, yet the new grass made it a green flag of survival.
Before rain the road was a drum; after the flood it was a mirror holding the clouds.
The verdict was a door: it shut the old case and opened the appeal that followed.
The committee was a wheel moving the plan forward and a cage holding that same plan motionless.
